title: Adic exceptional adjunction and compact-support projection formula
statement:
Let $k$ be any field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $R=\mathcal O_E$, $\varpi$ a uniformizer, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work with modules over $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ on the small pro-etale sites and their derived-complete bounded constructible categories [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and with completed pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], adic direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image], and compact support [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

There are exact $R$-linear constructible adjunctions $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ and $Rf_!\dashv f^!$. The exceptional functor preserves the indicated integral category and has canonical natural reductions
$$(f^!M)\otimes_R^LA_n\cong f_n^!(M\otimes_R^LA_n),$$
where $f_n^!$ is the bounded constructible exceptional adjoint on finite-coefficient etale categories, on the bounded constructible etale complexes of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], transported to the pro-etale site by the exact comparison pullback $\nu_T^*$ along $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The integral counit reduces to the finite counit. For $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and $M\in D^b_c(Y,R)$ the canonical projection map is an isomorphism
$$Rf_!(K\widehat\otimes_R^LLf^*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}(Rf_!K)\widehat\otimes_R^LM.$$
For composable separated finite-type maps $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, the compact-support composition isomorphism $Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$ and its right-adjoint mate $f^!g^!\cong(gf)^!$ hold on these integral categories; they satisfy identity and associativity equations. All these adjunctions, comparisons and projection maps commute with shifts. For a finite extension $E\subset L$ write $C_{L/E}K=K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ for integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. There are natural isomorphisms $C_{L/E}Lf^*\cong Lf^*C_{L/E}$, $C_{L/E}Rf_*\cong Rf_*C_{L/E}$ (adic direct images), $C_{L/E}Rf_!\cong Rf_!C_{L/E}$ and $C_{L/E}f^!\cong f^!C_{L/E}$, the last being the right-adjoint mate of the compact-support one. Each is the identity for $L=E$ and, for $E\subset L\subset L'$, satisfies the tower equation with the composition isomorphisms $C_{L'/L}C_{L/E}\cong C_{L'/E}$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. Under these isomorphisms and the tensor comparison of that lemma, scalar extension carries the units and counits of both adjunctions, the finite reductions, the composition isomorphisms and their mates, and the projection maps over $\mathcal O_E$ to the corresponding ones over $\mathcal O_L$.

source.place: Lemmas 6.7.2, 6.7.7, 6.7.14, 6.7.16–6.7.19 and Remark 6.8.15; composition from compactification and passage through the normalized finite-level tower

proof.text: Every scheme in a compactification of $f$ is finite type over $k$. Fields are excellent by [lem-exc-fields-excellent], and their finite-type algebras are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. Thus these schemes are quasi-excellent and $\ell$-coprime, as required in the source; no cohomological-dimension assumption on $k$ is being made. They are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] to identify precisely the integral category in the question, with its completed coefficient sheaf, with the source's constructible complete category. Finite reductions have bounded etale origins by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. For an integral object $P$, choose an interval $[a,b]$ bounding $P_1$. Tensor associativity gives $(P_n)\otimes^L_{A_n}A_1=P_1$. The etale residue test [lem-exc-residue-tor-test], transported by [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian], therefore gives Tor interval $[a,b]$ for all $P_n$. This supplies finite Tor without assuming it in the item.

source.place: §6.7 hypotheses; Definition 6.5.1, Proposition 6.6.11; finite Tor supplied by the residue criterion

proof.text: Use $\mathcal R_T$ and $\mathcal L_T$ for the coherent reduction and total-limit functors of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. For the constructible inputs at issue, $P\to\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_TP$ is the canonical invertible completion unit: [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies this category with the Koszul-complete constructible category, and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies that completion with the specified quotient-tower unit. This uses more than the object-only Roos-triangle definition of completeness. On normalized systems the counit $\mathcal R_T\mathcal L_TM\to M$ is invertible by [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] and is a system morphism by the evaluation calculus. Consequently $\mathcal R_T$ and $\mathcal L_T$ give inverse equivalences between complete integral objects and normalized derived systems: the unit and counit are the specified ones, and their triangle identities come from the stated reduction/limit adjunction. On the constructible subcategories, a normalized system with bounded constructible levels has uniformly bounded Tor intervals as soon as its level-one object is bounded: apply the two residue/comparison tests of step 1 to $M_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_1\cong M_1$. Effectivity and the defining uniform-reduction condition then put $\mathcal L_TM$ in $D^b_c(T,R)$. We will transport actual functors and transformations through this equivalence, never deduce equality of maps from equality of their individual reductions.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.19 reconstruction argument, with coherent reduction/total-limit adjunction made explicit

proof.text: Let $P_f,S_f$ be exact inverse image and total derived direct image on finite-coefficient systems. They form $P_f\dashv S_f$, with evaluated units and counits, by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. On bounded constructible etale complexes $Rf_{*,n}$ preserves bounded constructibility: [sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type] applies to each cohomology sheaf, and the finitely many truncation triangles give the assertion for the complex. The coefficient projection comparison for a quotient $A_m\to A_n$ is invertible by [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant]. Its finite-cohomological-dimension hypothesis follows from [lem-kun-0f10], uniformly for torsion coefficients. Restriction of coefficients identifies the output with $Rf_{*,n}$ by [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]; [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] transports the calculation between the two sites. Thus $S_f$ carries normalized constructible systems to normalized constructible systems. Their output level one is bounded, so step 2 supplies the required common interval. Pullback preservation and its finite comparisons are [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible]. The comparison [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] also identifies this adic direct image with ordinary ringed direct image on completed coefficient sheaves, with the same tower projections.

Conjugate $P_f\dashv S_f$ through the equivalences in step 2. Explicitly, for complete constructible $M,K$, fullness and faithfulness of these equivalences give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal L_XP_f\mathcal R_YM,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P_f\mathcal R_YM,\mathcal R_XK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal R_YM,S_f\mathcal R_XK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,\mathcal L_YS_f\mathcal R_XK).$$
These bijections are natural. Their left functor is the completed $Lf^*$ by [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution], and their right functor is exactly the adic $Rf_*$ of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], including its quotient transitions. The natural-bijection construction [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] gives the adjunction and both triangle identities. Its units and counits are conjugates of the system ones, rather than maps chosen independently at each level.

Fix one compactification $f=pj$. The finite compact-support functors have actual system realization $\mathcal F_f=S_pJ_j$ by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The proper etale projection formula [lem-etale-proper-projection-formula-finite], the open tensor identification [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], and [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] give, on finite constructible inputs,
$$F_nK_n\otimes^L_{A_n}M_n\xrightarrow{\sim}F_n(K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}f_n^*M_n).$$
Here the monoidal comparison for $\nu^*$ is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. In particular the same proper/open composite with the constant coefficient module $A_n$ gives normalization across $A_m\to A_n$. These maps are formed from tensor comparisons and the proper counit on the system category itself, as specified in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; their evaluation is the displayed finite map. Thus this is a coherent system transformation. The finite inputs and tensor products are bounded by the Tor intervals of step 1. Compact support preserves the integral category by [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible], and its defining total-limit tower is precisely $\mathcal L_Y\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_X$.

source.place: Definition 6.7.6, Lemmas 6.7.7, 6.7.14 and 6.7.16; finite proper/open projection construction

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-finite-exceptional-system-adjunction] on the etale coefficient systems. It supplies $\mathcal F_f\dashv\mathcal G_f$ on normalized finite-Tor constructible systems with the actual finite exceptional units and counits. Step 1 checks that $\mathcal R_YM$ belongs to its domain. Its output is normalized and has bounded constructible level one $G_1M_1$; the residue argument of step 2 therefore makes all its levels uniformly bounded. Transport this system and the adjunction to the pro-etale site by [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison] and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. This is legitimate on these bounded-below systems, whose bounds were just proved; the comparison counit is invertible, including the transition maps. The left functor becomes exactly the pro-etale $\mathcal F_f$ by [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. Define
$$f^!M=\mathcal L_X
u_X^*\mathcal G_fR
u_{Y,*}\mathcal R_YM.$$
All maps are images of maps of derived systems. Step 2 proves that this object is in the indicated integral category, with canonical reduction $
u_X^*G_nR
u_{Y,*}M_n=f_n^!M_n$.

source.place: Lemmas 6.7.18–6.7.19: normalized finite exceptional system, its effectivity and constructibility

proof.text:
The equivalences of step 2 and the system adjunction of step 6 give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!K,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_XK,\mathcal R_YM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal R_XK,\mathcal G_f\mathcal R_YM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,f^!M),$$
where the etale/pro-etale equivalences of step 6 are inserted in the middle terms. Use [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to obtain $Rf_!\dashv f^!$. Its counit is the total-limit image of the system counit, conjugated by the reduction/limit unit and counit. The triangle identities of that equivalence cancel the inserted comparisons; evaluation of the resulting system counit is the finite counit by [lem-per-finite-exceptional-system-adjunction]. This proves the asserted reduction of the specified integral counit, not just existence of an adjunction having isomorphic right-functor objects.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.19: adjunction and counit normalized by the finite exceptional adjunction

proof.text: Take the coherent projection transformation of step 5 and apply $\mathcal L_Y$. Its source is $(Rf_!K)\widehat\otimes^L_RM$ and its target is $Rf_!(K\widehat\otimes^L_RLf^*M)$: insert the coherent counits $\mathcal R\mathcal L\cong1$, then apply [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] to the tensor and pullback expressions. The source and target systems are normalized and the finite projection maps are invertible, so [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] makes the system projection an isomorphism before taking the limit. Its inverse realizes the direction displayed in the item. The projection map is the canonical one: it is the proper counit tensored with the identity followed by the open tensor comparison, all formed on the system category and transported with its adjunctions. Its finite reduction is therefore the finite canonical projection. This establishes both invertibility and normalization without treating finite evaluation as faithful on derived morphisms.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.14, integral projection from the canonical proper/open system map

proof.text: For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, choose compatible compactifications by [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle]: from one of $g$ it gives ones of $f$ and $gf$ with a cartesian proper/open square. On coefficient systems use the proper/open interchange and the direct-image and open-extension compositors. These are actual system maps with horizontal and vertical pasting identities by [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting]. Their finite evaluations are the canonical compact-support composition maps; [thm-sf-comp-composition] makes each evaluation invertible. Joint conservativity in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] then makes the system compositor invertible. After applying $\mathcal L$ and inserting $\mathcal R\mathcal L\cong1$ as in step 8, it gives $Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$. The system pasting equations give its identity and associativity equations before total limit. Take its adjunction conjugate to get $f^!g^!\cong(gf)^!$. The mate-pasting equations [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identify the two triple composites and identity mates, so the right-adjoint compositors satisfy exactly the corresponding equations.

source.place: Compactification composition; system pasting before passage to total limit

proof.text: All reductions, system inverse images, open extensions and scalar tensors are derived from additive functors and total complexes. Their shift comparisons are termwise cochain shifts with the usual tensor signs. Total derived inverse limit is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Hence the transported pullback, direct image and compact support are exact $R$-linear functors. The system exceptional functor in [lem-per-finite-exceptional-system-adjunction] is exact and $R$-linear, so its transported $f^!$ is too. The canonical right-adjoint shift is the unique one compatible with the unit and counit by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique]. Thus both adjunctions commute with shifts. Projection, reduction and composition maps commute with those comparisons: on simultaneous resolutions they are composites of the termwise shift-compatible unit, counit and signed tensor maps. The tensor substitution theorem [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] carries their signed system comparisons to the completed ones. This also checks shift compatibility for the exceptional mates by mate pasting.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15, exact six functors; derived shift and mate normalizations

proof.text:
Let $S=\mathcal O_L$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat S_T$ is finite free over $\widehat R_T$, and the scalar functor in the question is ordinary derived tensor with this sheaf. Pullback and tensor comparisons with scalar extension, including their identity and tower equations, are [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. For direct image use the coherent comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. This applies because the schemes are Noetherian and finite-dimensional, and step 3 proved direct-image constructibility. For compact support, [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison] and [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] identify its defining tower with the separately derived composite $Rp_*j_!$. Use a single compactification: the direct-image comparison for $p$ and the coefficient version of the open tensor comparison [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] give
$$C_YRp_*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*C_{\overline X}j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*j_!C_X.$$
These are the same comparisons on strict reduction systems. At ramification index $e$, $S/t^nS=S/v^{en}$. The canonical restriction of total limits to these levels, with all projection maps and units, is [lem-sp-strict-tower-arithmetic-restriction]. Thus the displayed comparison realizes $C_YRf_!\cong Rf_!C_X$ for exactly the compact-support definition in the question, even for ramified extensions.

source.place: Definition 6.7.6 and Remark 6.8.15; finite-free coefficient extension and cofinal uniformizer powers

proof.text:
Write $F_R=Rf_{!,R}$ and $G_R=f_R^!$, with the analogous $S$-functors, and let $q:C_YF_R\cong F_SC_X$ be step 11. Define $b:C_XG_R\to G_SC_Y$ to be the $F_S\dashv G_S$ transpose of $C_Y\epsilon_R\circ q_{G_R}^{-1}$. To check invertibility, restriction of scalars $V$ is right adjoint to $C$ by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. $V$ preserves the constructible categories: it is exact, keeps cohomology sheaves, and $\widehat S_T=\widehat R_T\otimes_RS$ (limit of $(R/t^n)_T\otimes_RS=(S/t^nS)_T$, $S$ finite free over $R$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]), so criterion (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] passes to $V$. Thus, naturally in $N,K$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(K,V_XG_SN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_XK,G_SN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_SC_XK,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_YF_RK,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_RK,V_YN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,G_RV_YN).$$
Applying this natural bijection and its inverse to the identity maps gives mutually inverse maps (naturality proves the two composites are identities). The resulting comparison identifies $V_XG_S$ with $G_RV_Y$, with its counit. Under this identification the underlying map of $b_M$ is $G_RM\otimes_RS\to G_R(M\otimes_RS)$. Choose an $R$-basis of $S$ just to test it. This becomes the canonical map from the finite direct sum of copies of $G_RM$ to $G_R$ of that finite direct sum. Its components are $G_R$ of the inclusions, as follows by transposing the defining formula for $b$. Additivity of $G_R$ makes it invertible. Restriction of scalars detects isomorphisms since it leaves cohomology sheaves unchanged. Therefore $b$ is an isomorphism, canonically the mate specified in the question; its construction did not choose a basis.

source.place: Finite-free coefficient change for the exceptional adjoint; explicit agent adjunction argument

proof.text:
For either adjunction, the coefficient comparison carries its counit to the extended counit: for the exceptional pair this is the defining transpose equation
$$\epsilon_S\circ F_Sb\circ q_{G_R}=C_Y\epsilon_R.$$
The unit equation follows by substituting this equation in the inverse adjunction bijection and using both triangle identities. For the ordinary pair, compute the direct-image coefficient map on a chosen $R$-basis of $S$: it is the canonical finite-sum comparison, and the pullback coefficient map is tensor reassociation. The extended adjunction bijection is consequently the direct sum of the original bijections. It sends the identity to the extended unit and the inverse bijection sends the identity to the extended counit; naturality makes this basis computation an identity for the canonical maps. Its compatibility with completed pullback is tensor reassociation on the reduction systems, so the same triangle argument applies. Quotient coefficient maps satisfy that reassociation identity too; hence these equations carry every finite reduction and its finite counit to the corresponding maps after coefficient extension. Identity extensions give identity tensor maps. For $E\subset L\subset L'$, the two successive scalar maps agree with the single scalar map because both send $(x\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $x\otimes st$. The open maps satisfy the same equality by their restriction-to-the-open normalization, and direct-image maps by their adjunction transpose. Mate pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] gives the tower equation for $b$, and the corresponding unit equations. These arguments occur on the strict coefficient diagrams before total inverse limit.

source.place: Coefficient extension of adjunction equations and quotient diagrams; agent normalization check

proof.text: Finally every compact-support compositor of step 9 is the proper/open mate word in its units, counits, open comparisons and direct-image compositors. Every projection of step 8 is the proper counit tensored with the identity followed by the open tensor map. Step 13 carries these individual factors and their adjunction transposes to the factors over $S$; the tensor comparison is the one in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. Therefore it carries the entire ordered composites to the specified composites over $S$. The proper/open pasting identities in [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting] and the abstract mate-pasting equations show the same assertion for the right-adjoint composition mates. Taking total limits preserves these equations because they are equations of actual system maps. This proves scalar compatibility of composition, its exceptional mate, projection, both adjunctions and finite reductions, with their identity, tower and shift normalizations. The zero objects, empty schemes, identity morphisms and $L=E$ are included: all their displayed system maps are the relevant identities or zero maps.

source.place: Composition and projection normalizations after scalar change; agent check on the specified mate words
